title: flags: fix broken roff bold markup in --null-data docs
body:
The long help for `--null-data` (`crates/core/flags/defs.rs:5407`) opens bold with `\fP` instead of `\fB`:

```
of the default of \fP\\n\fP.
```

`\fP` restores the previous font; with no preceding `\fB` on that line it's a no-op, so `\\n` renders un-bolded in the generated man page. Every other reference to `\\n` in this file uses the correct `\fB\\n\fP` pair, and this is the only `\fP\\` in the whole crate.

**Repro** (verified locally):
- Before: `rg --generate man` emitted `of the default of \fP\\n\fP.`
- After: `of the default of \fB\\n\fP.` (`grep '\fP\\n'` on generated man → 0 matches)

Help-text/markup change only; no behavior change. `cargo build` clean.

title: globset: note that nested brace alternates are allowed
body:
## Problem

The globset crate's top-level syntax docs (`crates/globset/src/lib.rs`) still say:

> `{a,b}` ... (N.B. Nesting `{...}` is not currently allowed.)

This is stale. Nested brace alternates are supported:

- The `ErrorKind::NestedAlternates` variant in the very same file is documented as **DEPRECATED**: *"This error used to occur when an alternating group was nested inside another alternating group, e.g., `{{a,b},{c,d}}`. However, this is now supported and as such this error cannot occur."*
- The parser (`push_alternate`/`pop_alternate`) uses a stack and never emits `NestedAlternates`.
- Tests confirm it: `toregex!(re36, "{a,{b,c}}", ...)`, `toregex!(re37, "{{a,b},{c,d}}", ...)`, and `matches!(matchalt17..19, "{a,b{c,d}}", ...)`.

## Change

Update the stale note so it matches the actual behaviour and the `NestedAlternates` deprecation. Docs-only; no logic change.

## Verification

`cargo test -p globset` → 290 passed, 0 failed; doctests compile cleanly with the change.

---

title: printer: fix hyperlink paths that are not valid UTF-8
body:
on unix a path can contain bytes that aren't valid UTF-8. `HyperlinkPath::encode` copied every byte >= 128 as is, so the URI wasn't valid and raw bytes ended up inside the OSC 8 sequence.

bytes that aren't part of valid UTF-8 are now percent-encoded (the loop goes over `utf8_chunks()`). valid non-ascii is still left unencoded like before, since encoding it breaks file:// URLs on windows (as the doc comment on `encode` says). nothing changes on windows, the path is always valid UTF-8 there.

added `encode_invalid_utf8` and a CHANGELOG entry. grep-printer tests pass.

Fixes #3526

title: printer: don't emit reset sequences for `none` color specs
body:
with a spec like `--colors path:none` the printers still called `set_color` and `reset`, which writes `\x1b[0m` on both sides of the field. invisible in a terminal, but noise for anything parsing the output.

empty specs are now skipped, like the standard printer already does for matched lines. this covers paths, line numbers, columns and byte offsets in the standard printer, paths in the summary printer and `--files`, and matches in multi-line mode.

`r599` expected `\x1b[0m1\x1b[0m:`, I updated it to `1:` (its comment already says useless escape sequences are no longer emitted). one small behaviour change: with `-U`, `match:none` and a `highlight` background, the highlight now continues through the match instead of being reset there.

4 new tests, grep-printer and integration tests pass, CHANGELOG entry added.

Fixes #3289

title: After reading all ignore files (global & local), `ripgrep` should include all tracked files no matter what
body: So today I noticed a pattern was not found when I ran `rg`. The pattern is available in a `shell.nix` file which I ignore globally in `~/.config/git/ignore`, but I added it a long time ago to my current repo with `git add --force shell.nix`. I wonder, why does `rg` reads the git ignore files by itself, and doesn't simply consult `git ls-files`? Maybe the `git ls-files` list should be added after the ignore files are treated?

title: globset,ignore: exclude path separator from character classes when li…
body:
Closes #2745

### Motivation
When `literal_separator(true)` is enabled in `globset` (used by `ignore` for `.gitignore` matching), directory separators (`/`) should not be matched by bracket expressions/character classes (`[...]`), following Git wildmatch and POSIX `fnmatch(..., FNM_PATHNAME)` semantics.

Previously, if a character class contained `/` (such as `*[\<\>\:\"\/\\\|\?\*]*` used to filter Windows-invalid filename characters) or was negated (e.g. `[^a]`), `globset` allowed the class to match across `/`. This caused patterns intended for filenames to unexpectedly match directory paths like `folder/bar.txt` and ignore valid files.

### Changes
1. **`globset::glob`**:
   - When `literal_separator` is true and a class is non-negated, exclude `/` from ranges (splitting ranges like `' '..='~'` that cross `/`). If no characters remain, emit a pattern that matches nothing (`[^\s\S]`).
   - When `negated` is true, explicitly add `/` to the negated set (`[^/...]`) so it will not match `/`.
   - Updated `matchslash4` in `glob.rs` to reflect that `abc[/]def` does not match `abc/def` under `SLASHLIT`.
2. **`ignore::gitignore`**:
   - Added a regression test verifying the pattern from #2745 does not ignore files in subdirectories.

title: cli: use split_at() in parse_human_readable_size()
body:
Replace two separate slice operations (`&size[..digits_end]` and `&size[digits_end..]`) with a single `split_at(digits_end)` call.

The Rust compiler has a dedicated optimization for `split_at()` that emits only one bounds check and fewer instructions compared to two independent slices (verified with cargo asm on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu).

This function is not hot code, so the performance difference is negligible. But it uses a standard library function so it is arguably more idiomatic and readable.

title: fix(ignore): keep excluded ancestor ignored despite path whitelist
body:
Relates-to: #3538. Complements #3541 (docs-only, no behavior change).

Walks parents of an excluded dir so a conflicting allow rule on an ancestor cannot re-include paths beneath it. Verified: new regression test fails with the fix reverted and passes with it applied; full ignore suite 182/182 green; behavior cross-checked against git check-ignore as oracle.

title: pattern: report file and line numbers for pattern compilation errors
body:
When loading patterns from `-f` / `--file` (or stdin), a regex compilation failure previously printed the syntax error against the composite alternation without indicating which file or line number contained the invalid pattern.

This change:
- Tracks 1-based line numbers when reading patterns from readers/files/stdin in `grep-cli`.
- Attaches origin information (`PatternOrigin::File { path, line }` / `PatternOrigin::Stdin { line }`) to loaded patterns.
- When regex compilation fails, isolates the offending pattern by compiling each pattern individually and prefixes the error message with `{path}:{line}:` or `<stdin>:{line}:`. This fallback loop only executes on the `Err` path, so successful compilations incur no runtime penalty.
- Adds integration tests verifying single and multiple `-f` error reporting.

Closes #478.

title: regex: honor custom line terminators in the regex engine
body:
`--null-data --no-mmap` was going through the slow line-by-line searcher. therefore a file of nuls with one needle in the middle was walking every nul as its own empty record.

grep-regex never told the regex engine about the configured terminator, and hence `(?m:^)` / `(?m:$)` only understood `\n`. the searcher worked around that by disabling the fast path when the terminator was nul. actually that workaround is what made the search so slow.

i passed the terminator through to regex-automata. `--null-data` still means nul-separated records, and `--line-regexp` still matches a whole record. a grep-searcher test counts matcher calls on a nul-heavy haystack so we can see the fast path is in use.

Fixes #2832

title: ignore: note git divergence in matched_path_or_any_parents docs
body:
`matched_path_or_any_parents` returns as soon as the path itself matches, including a whitelist. That means a path under an ignored directory can show up as not ignored here, while `git check-ignore` still ignores it.

This only updates the doc-comment so callers don't treat the method as a drop-in git equivalent. No behavior change.

Fixes #3538

title: Add end columns to --vimgrep output
body:
This PR adds end-column information to "--vimgrep" output

Previously --vimgrep emitted:
```
file:line:column:text
```
It now emits:
```
file:line:column:end_column:text
```
The end column is derived from the match end offset and allows Vim to populate the quickfix "end_col" field when using:
```
:set grepformat=%f:%l:%c:%k:%m
```
This also updates the existing vimgrep tests and adds coverage for UTF-8 matches,  --no-column and multiline matches.

Also fixes #3532

title: ignore: ignore empty gitignore negation patterns
body:
Fixes #3527

### Summary

A bare `!` in a `.gitignore` pattern was parsed as an empty pattern after
the negation prefix was stripped.

The empty pattern then fell through to glob construction and was expanded
to `**/` with whitelist semantics, causing the bare `!` to match entries.

Git treats a negation with no remaining pattern as a no-op.

This change:

- returns early when the pattern becomes empty after stripping `!`/`/`
- preserves normal negation patterns
- adds regression coverage for `!`, `!/`, ordering, and escaped `\!`

### Testing

- `cargo test -p ignore`
- `cargo test -p globset`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p ignore --all-targets`
- `git diff --check`
- `cargo test -p ripgrep --test integration`

title: ignore: matched_path_or_any_parents doesn't skip excluded ancestors, and the doc-comment doesn't say so
body:
`matched_path_or_any_parents` returns as soon as the *full* path matches a rule — whitelist included — and only walks up to the parents when the path itself matched nothing (`gitignore.rs:234`). git never descends into an excluded directory, so a negation under one rescues nothing. Three rules files, `git check-ignore --no-index` (2.55.0) as the oracle, path asked for the way the API wants it (no trailing slash, `is_dir` passed separately):

| rules | path | git | `matched_path_or_any_parents` | `matched` | `rg --files` 14.1.1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dist/` + `!*.pub` | `dist/keep.pub` | ignored | not ignored | not ignored | not listed ✓ |
| `.idea/` + `!.idea/eclipseCodeFormatter.xml` | `.idea/eclipseCodeFormatter.xml` | ignored | not ignored | not ignored | not listed ✓ |
| `__tmp/` + `!__tmp/keep` | `__tmp/keep` | ignored | not ignored | not ignored | not listed ✓ |

Scale, so it isn't three hand-made trees: over 9,852 (rules file, path) queries taken from the root `.gitignore` of 43 real repositories, `matched_path_or_any_parents` diverges from git on **63**, and all 63 are that one shape and that one direction — git ignores, the crate doesn't. They're a strict subset of the 1,976 that plain `matched` gets wrong on the same corpus, so the parents walk is never *worse*, it just doesn't cover this. The walk isn't affected, as the last column shows.

I'm not asking for a behaviour change. Getting this right means knowing which directory the rules file governs and whether each ancestor is excluded, and that's the walk's job, not this method's. What I'd ask for is a line in the doc-comment, because #1715 and #2857 both end with the reporter adopting this method as *the* git-equivalent one and the limit isn't written anywhere.

Before filing I went looking for a consumer it actually bites, and I owe you the negative result: `cargo` isn't one. Five package trees, `cargo package --list --allow-dirty` inside a real repo with a commit — it excludes the re-included file in all five, matching git. (The control row, same trees with the negation removed, changes answer, so the ignore is genuinely being applied and the test isn't vacuous.) `rustfmt` does call it on bare paths (`ignore_path.rs:27`), but over `rustfmt.toml`'s own `ignore` list rather than a `.gitignore`, where the divergence does no harm. So: a documented-behaviour gap I can measure, not a fire.

Corpus, adapter and the exact queries: https://github.com/KaizenShogun/gitignore-conformance

title: ignore/types: add ninja type
body: Adds a `-t` flag for https://ninja-build.org/ files.

title: hyperlink: percent-encode invalid UTF-8 bytes in file URLs
body:
Hyperlink path encoding copied every byte >= 0x80 raw into the OSC 8 URL, so filenames with undecodable bytes (e.g. 0xFF) produced raw non-UTF-8 output in the terminal sequence.

This keeps valid UTF-8 sequences as-is (IRI behavior per RFC 8089, matching UrlCreateFromPathW on Windows) and percent-encodes only bytes that cannot form valid UTF-8: lone continuations, truncated sequences, overlongs, surrogates, and 0xF5-0xFF. The --hyperlink-format docs are softened to match. Covered by a new unit test (encode_percent_encodes_invalid_utf8); I could not run an invalid-byte end-to-end test on APFS, which rejects such filenames, so unit coverage is the proof here.

Fixes #3526.

> Note: I used an AI coding assistant for drafting; the change and description above are my own and I have verified the tests.

title: ignore: detect symlink loops above the search root
body:
Currently `check_symlink_loop` only considers directories below the starting directory. The recursive walk happily follows links to directories above that, including to `/`. I discovered this when vscode used ripgrep to search for `**/node_modules` in a project directory that contained a WINEPREFIX, including the typical `Z:\`->`/` symlink. A few minutes later it had found 10k+ invalid matches all over my filesystem and emitted two million lines to stderr about /proc and /dev access failures, and I only noticed because it was maxing out 8 CPU cores.

This PR takes advantage of the existing `add_parents` which already walks the ancestor directories looking for things like `.gitignore`. `--follow` is added to the triggers for that walk, one dead getter is removed, and relevant supporting changes are made.

There are three new tests included. I considered trying to get them working on Windows, but decided not to since I don't have a Windows machine and the existing symlink tests are already unix-only.

This fixes the parallel walker only. The single-threaded `Walk` delegates loop detection to `walkdir`. See https://github.com/BurntSushi/walkdir/pull/220

The code and commit message for this PR were authored approximately 50% by Claude Opus 5.
